input.question: Why can't Social Security Numbers be like credit card numbers where they get renewed (new number) every couple of years and if they get lost or stolen the old number can be cancelled and you get a new number?
input.ground_truth: The problem is that your Social Security Number is widely used as a *unique identifier* for a person. The whole reason it's worth stealing is because everyone uses the same number to reference a person. If you just get a new number every few years, it'd either be worthless for a credit report **or** somebody would just have a list of all your previous SSNs matched up against your current one and you'd have to tell everyone who uses it to update to your new number anyways. The fundamental issue is that the SSN was never intended to be a general purpose citizen identification number, it was just meant to be used for a single government program. Security was never even a concern in designing the system. If you want a safe & secure system for identifying a person, you'd need to approach the problem completely differently.

Okay, let’s imagine Social Security Numbers (SSNs) are like your special library card at school. This card helps the library know which books are yours.

Now, imagine if you lost your library card or someone else found it and took your books. If you could get a new library card every few years, it would be easier to keep your books safe. If you lose the old card, you can get a new one and tell the library to stop letting anyone use the old one.

But, right now, your Social Security Number is like a library card that never changes. Lots of important grown-up things use this number—like getting a job, going to the doctor, or getting money when you’re older. If everyone got a new SSN every few years, it would be very confusing for all the grown-ups and computers that need to find your information.

Also, changing everyone’s number would take a lot of time and work. So, instead of changing the number, we try to keep it safe and only share it with people we trust.

But it’s a good idea that some people talk about, just like how some people think the library should let you change your library card number if you lose it!
